Open pull request proposes changes for review. These are distinct actions. Inspect the destination and visible result before confirming.
steps.checkpoint: The repository, privacy and proposed change are the ones you intended.

steps.title: Get updates and review the result
steps.narrationDraft: Get updates brings remote changes into a connected local folder. Conflicts may need attention when both copies changed. Open the GitHub result to verify the upload or pull request. Posting a code review to GitHub shares it with people who can see that pull request.
steps.checkpoint: You can find the final repository or pull request and check its contents.

lessons.title: Connect your phone or Telegram
lessons.prerequisites: Genesis running on the computer. Android app for pairing, or a Telegram bot token for Telegram.

steps.title: Your computer is still the engine
steps.narrationDraft: The phone app and Telegram can talk to the desktop Genesis. They do not move the whole AI, models or memory onto the phone. Keep the computer’s Genesis running and reachable. A phone connection and a Telegram connection are separate setup choices.
steps.checkpoint: You understand where the model and work are running.

steps.title: Pair the Android app
steps.narrationDraft: Use Pair Mobile Device in the left panel or the phone step in Finish setting up. Follow the displayed pairing flow in the Android app. Treat the pairing information as private. Confirm the intended device is connected before asking it to control desktop work.
steps.checkpoint: Your intended phone completes pairing.

steps.title: Connect a Telegram bot
steps.narrationDraft: Open Settings → Communications. Get a bot token through Telegram’s BotFather, enter it in Bot token, enable the bridge and save. Open your bot in Telegram and press Start. The page’s status shows whether the bridge has connected.
steps.checkpoint: Your bot replies and the desktop shows it connected.

steps.title: Restrict who may control the bot
steps.narrationDraft: Check Allowed users. After messaging the bot, the Allow only… action can restrict control to your chat. An empty list uses the first chat that messages it, so explicitly restricting the intended chat is clearer for an unattended setup.
steps.checkpoint: Only the intended Telegram user may control Genesis.

steps.title: Choose how much reaches Telegram
steps.narrationDraft: Activity on Telegram offers Silent, Status and Verbose. Status edits one live activity card; Verbose sends more steps. Telegram alert controls can mute sounds or temporarily pause alerts. /unplug disconnects the bridge; you can enable it again from Genesis.
steps.checkpoint: The phone receives the amount of activity you intended.

steps.title: Answer a needs-you request once
steps.narrationDraft: Approvals, codes and challenges can reach the desktop, paired phone and Telegram. The first valid answer wins. Optional email-code reading and phone SMS-code forwarding have separate settings and permissions. Start with manual answers until you understand those options.
steps.checkpoint: You know where to answer a request and which connections receive it.

lessons.title: When Genesis needs your help
lessons.prerequisites: An action or mission that has requested owner input.

steps.title: Read the request before answering
steps.narrationDraft: Discoveries and the connected communication surfaces can show requests for help. Read what action is proposed, its destination and the result it expects. Approve only the actual action you intend. An ambiguous request is a good reason to ask for clarification.
steps.checkpoint: You can state exactly what you are approving.

steps.title: Keep sign-in and verification deliberate
steps.narrationDraft: A site may need a login, verification code or CAPTCHA. Complete the required step through the offered handoff. Genesis does not solve a CAPTCHA for you. A code request should belong to the sign-in you expect, not an unrelated message.
steps.checkpoint: The correct request is answered on the intended site.

steps.title: Decline or explain a different choice
steps.narrationDraft: If the request is wrong, decline it and explain the change you want. If it simply needs more facts, answer those facts. An approval is specific to the request; it is not a blanket promise that all later actions are approved.
steps.checkpoint: Your decision accurately expresses what you want next.

steps.title: Check the final deliverable
steps.narrationDraft: Projects wait in Review and missions have owner sign-off. Open the actual file, page or result before accepting. A model saying “finished” is not the same as your acceptance. If it falls short, describe the missing result in plain words.
steps.checkpoint: You accept work based on its result.

lessons.title: Keep a small companion on your desktop
lessons.prerequisites: The Genesis desktop app on Windows.

steps.title: Open Desktop pet
steps.narrationDraft: Open Settings → Computer use → Desktop pet, or View → Mini & Pets. The page shows the pets available in your version. Choose the one you like and turn on Show pet on desktop, or click Show mini. These desktop preferences apply immediately.
steps.checkpoint: The selected pet appears on your desktop.

steps.title: Use its little controls
steps.narrationDraft: Drag its handle to move it. The small chat, voice and menu controls give quick access to Genesis. The pet is a doorway into the same app, not a separate model or a new memory.
steps.checkpoint: You know how to move it and open Genesis.

steps.title: Show or hide it when convenient
steps.narrationDraft: Use the page’s Show/Hide mini control. The shortcut shown in Settings can focus the pet when available; if another app owns the shortcut, use Show mini instead. The selected desktop pet can return at the next Genesis start.
steps.checkpoint: You can show and hide the companion without losing your conversation.

lessons.title: Give file tools the right working folder
lessons.prerequisites: Settings → System → Tool access. Know the folder your task needs.

steps.title: Find the workspace
steps.narrationDraft: Workspace shows Genesis’s normal working folder. It follows the installation automatically. Ask Genesis to put a result there when you do not need a different location. This is separate from adding a Git folder under Code.
steps.checkpoint: You can locate the folder where ordinary outputs belong.

steps.title: Allow another folder only when needed
steps.narrationDraft: Additional allowed write paths lists other folders the file tools may write to, one path per line. Add the exact project folder your intended task needs, then save. Do not add the whole computer simply to silence an error. Permissions and service connections are separate layers.
steps.checkpoint: The allowed path is the specific folder you intended.

steps.title: Protect important files
steps.narrationDraft: Protected files names files that should be kept protected from tool writes. Core read-only protects Genesis’s core identity from its own modification. These controls apply to supported tool paths; they are not an operating-system sandbox for every third-party program or shell command.
steps.checkpoint: You understand which tool boundary the setting provides.

steps.title: Give commands enough time
steps.narrationDraft: Bash timeout (s) limits how long a shell command may run through that tool. A long build may need more time than a short listing. Change a timeout for a known need, save, and inspect the actual command result. A longer timeout does not repair a wrong command.
steps.checkpoint: You can distinguish a timed-out command from a model connection problem.

lessons.title: Understand what Genesis remembers
lessons.prerequisites: Settings → Memory. Use ordinary chat for a gentle first example.

steps.title: Memory and the chat thread are different
steps.narrationDraft: A conversation is the visible exchange. Long-term memory holds selected information across conversations. Genesis can keep experiences, facts, procedures and active work notes. It does not retain every sentence with perfect recall, and it can make a mistake about an old event.
steps.checkpoint: You can distinguish a new chat from deleting memory.

steps.title: Say clearly what should be remembered
steps.narrationDraft: Try “Remember that I prefer short shopping lists.” Later ask “What do you remember about how I like shopping lists?” For an important detail, check the saved or recalled result. Correct a wrong fact explicitly: “That date is wrong; the correct date is…”
steps.checkpoint: Genesis recalls the intended preference correctly.

steps.title: Browse memory when you need to check
steps.narrationDraft: The Memory page lets you inspect available memory information. Search for a concrete phrase. A summary may be shorter than the original event. Recent and older memories can coexist until a correction is identified; a new statement is not automatically a universal replacement for every similar memory.
steps.checkpoint: You can look for the relevant memory and check it.

steps.title: Health and upkeep
steps.narrationDraft: Settings → Memory → Health → Check checks the store’s health. Sleep, rest and consolidation can organise recent material. The memory options are advanced tuning; leave defaults when starting. Do not use deletion, re-embedding or migration as a routine response to one mistaken answer.
steps.checkpoint: You know where the health check is and when to use it.

steps.title: Keep a complete backup
steps.narrationDraft: Use the Backups section for a complete saved copy of Genesis data. A code snapshot is different. Before a major move or memory operation, check that the backup reports complete. The next lesson covers what the backup and transfer controls actually do.
steps.checkpoint: You know how to protect memory before making a larger change.

lessons.title: Back up Genesis or move computers
lessons.prerequisites: Settings → Memory and enough disk space for a backup.

steps.title: Make a backup now
steps.narrationDraft: Open Settings → Memory → Backups and click Back up now. Wait for the result. A complete backup captures the personal data supported by the backup system. The page shows the stored archives and their location.
steps.checkpoint: The result explicitly says the backup is complete.

steps.title: An incomplete backup needs attention
steps.narrationDraft: If the result says INCOMPLETE, treat it as incomplete. The memory store may not have copied consistently. The previous complete archive is kept; try again when the system is idle. A ZIP file merely existing is not the same as a verified complete backup.
steps.checkpoint: You can identify a complete archive in the list.

steps.title: Keep a copy outside this computer
steps.narrationDraft: Copy a complete archive to a storage location you control. Automatic backups are useful but still live on the same computer unless you copy them elsewhere. Check the displayed backup path before looking for the file.
steps.checkpoint: You have a complete archive on separate storage.

steps.title: Use transfer options for a move
steps.narrationDraft: The Move to another computer section can prepare a transfer package. Read which data, workspace files and secrets you include. Secrets are sensitive and may need platform-specific handling. On the new installation, use the import flow for the transfer or supported old Genesis folder.
steps.checkpoint: The package includes the data you actually want to move.

steps.title: Restoration is not an in-app one-click undo
steps.narrationDraft: The Backups panel states that restoring is done with Genesis closed using the supported restore script. If you are not comfortable with that step, get help with the specific complete archive and destination. Do not restore over a running memory store or guess a data path.
steps.checkpoint: You know that creating a backup and restoring it are separate operations.

lessons.title: Read activity and usage
lessons.prerequisites: Some recorded activity in the current Genesis version.

steps.title: Open the Activity page
steps.narrationDraft: Click Activity in the left panel. It shows local usage totals, task duration, streaks and top tools. Recording begins with the version that provides this feature; it does not recreate a complete history from old chats.
steps.checkpoint: You can see the usage page and its recording period.

steps.title: Explore the calendar
steps.narrationDraft: Choose Daily, Weekly or Cumulative and click a calendar day. Daily is that day’s usage; Weekly groups a week; Cumulative adds usage over time. A quiet day can be normal if Genesis was not running tasks.
steps.checkpoint: You can switch the calendar view and inspect a day.

steps.title: Measured and estimated are different
steps.narrationDraft: A provider may report token counts; Genesis may estimate when it does not. Read those labels. These counters are local activity telemetry, not a billing invoice or a definitive remaining provider quota. Check your provider’s account for its charges and account limits.
steps.checkpoint: You can recognise the limits of the usage numbers.

steps.title: Context and logs answer different questions
steps.narrationDraft: The right-hand Activity & context panel describes the current request and tool state. System Feed, the conversation’s Activity / Log, and expandable tool rows help explain what happened. A busy indicator or low context number alone does not prove a task succeeded.
steps.checkpoint: You know which view to open for current work versus historical totals.

lessons.title: When something does not work
lessons.prerequisites: The relevant Genesis window and the exact error message, if present.

steps.title: Start with the exact visible state

anchor.label: Using backup: Qwen3 8B (Ollama). Next request will retry primary.

steps.narrationDraft: Read the status and error text. Is it disconnected, downloading, waiting for you, paused, thinking, or using backup? Copy the error and say what you clicked. Those details help much more than changing several settings at once.
steps.checkpoint: You can describe the observed problem in one sentence.

steps.title: If the model does not answer
steps.narrationDraft: Check the selected primary. For a local model, check the running service, address, model name and available memory. For a cloud model, check internet, key, model access and provider quota. A configured backup may continue some failures. A full context or task step limit needs a different response.
steps.checkpoint: The connection details match the chosen model.

steps.title: If voice is wrong or silent
steps.narrationDraft: For poor recognition, check microphone, languages and the In use now Whisper size. For silence, check the selected speaking engine, installed voice, mute state and key if cloud. The microphone and speaker can be muted independently in the orb. Try one short test after each change.
steps.checkpoint: You have isolated listening or speaking as the problem.

steps.title: If an image is not understood
steps.narrationDraft: Check that the main model or secondary preset genuinely supports images. Read Effective route, save any edits, and ask for a simple image description. A text-only model without a helper cannot interpret pixels. A cloud helper needs its own valid connection.
steps.checkpoint: A simple image works before you try a dense screen.

steps.title: If work pauses or remains unfinished
steps.narrationDraft: Read the plan, mission blockers and any needs-you request. Reply to the pending question or resume the correct paused loop. A new question does not automatically mean you wanted old unfinished work restarted. State “Continue the earlier task” when that is your intent.
steps.checkpoint: You know why the work stopped and which task should continue.

steps.title: Use Help and keep your evidence
steps.narrationDraft: Open Help → Help index, How-to guides or Finish setting up…. When asking for help, include the model/provider, exact error, steps taken and relevant tool output. Remove private keys and unrelated personal information before sharing. Make a complete backup before a repair involving personal data.
steps.checkpoint: You have enough information to request focused help.

lessons.title: Understand work limits, sleep and rest
lessons.prerequisites: Settings → System. Keep a working configuration before experimenting.

steps.title: Sleep is a maintenance state
steps.narrationDraft: In continuous modes, Genesis can pause for rest or sleep to organise memory and manage its working load. The visible state and timer explain this. It is part of the software’s operation; you do not need to interpret a mood number as proof of human feelings. Ordinary Chat is driven by your messages.
steps.checkpoint: You can recognise sleep as a deliberate maintenance state.

steps.title: Zero means the usual setting
steps.narrationDraft: The wide sliders use 0 for the usual setting. Move left for slower load growth or shorter sleep, depending on that slider; move right for the opposite. Read the live explanation beside each one. Each slider has its own purpose—“higher” is not automatically “better”.
steps.checkpoint: You can read the effect before saving a change.

steps.title: Know the four pace controls
steps.narrationDraft: Cognitive load speed controls how quickly load builds. Tool load influence adds the effect of failed tools and hard loops. Sleep length changes a sleep’s length; Rest length changes a short rest when micro-rests are enabled. Keep defaults until you have observed a specific problem.
steps.checkpoint: You know which control relates to your observation.

steps.title: Sleep thresholds and quiet hours
steps.narrationDraft: Sleep threshold decides when load triggers sleep. Waking span, Sleep share and Max sleep tune the work/sleep balance. Wake when rested may end a sleep early after consolidation; Sleep in my quiet hours adjusts timing around chat habits. Take micro-rests is a separate optional older behaviour.
steps.checkpoint: You understand the trade-off between time working and time maintaining memory.

steps.title: A step budget limits a turn, not a provider account
steps.narrationDraft: In Mode step budgets, Chat steps, Work steps and Autonomy steps limit reasoning/tool steps per turn or cycle. Higher budgets let one job do more and can use more tokens. They are different from provider rate limits and context size. A change applies to the next turn or cycle.
steps.checkpoint: You can distinguish a work budget from a cloud usage quota.

steps.title: Managed work waits when the job is done
steps.narrationDraft: Work policy → Managed waits without new inference when assigned work is finished. Continuous continues making useful work. Choose Managed for a bounded assignment while learning. Save an intended change and check the visible mode and status; the mission recovery choices belong to Missions separately.
steps.checkpoint: Your Work policy matches whether you want it to wait or continue.

lessons.title: A gentle tour of advanced memory options
lessons.prerequisites: Settings → Memory. A complete backup before any migration or re-embedding.

steps.title: Recall is choosing what to bring back
steps.narrationDraft: Memory-first recall refreshes relevant memories during multi-step work. Recalls per step controls how many are brought forward; Deliberate pacing adds a reminder to reason from them before acting. More recall can mean a larger context or slower work. It is not a guarantee that the right fact will be found.
steps.checkpoint: You understand why adding more memories is not always better.

steps.title: Capacity and retention are different
steps.narrationDraft: Memory tier caps limit how much each memory store holds. Episodic means experiences; semantic means facts; procedural means methods. Working capacity and Scratch note TTL concern temporary working notes. Capacity is storage space; retention also depends on use, relevance and the forgetting rules.
steps.checkpoint: You can distinguish stored knowledge from temporary working notes.

steps.title: The attention gate chooses lasting material
steps.narrationDraft: Gate threshold controls how salient an event must be to become lasting episodic memory. A less salient event can remain only as a fading working note. Flashbulb threshold helps strongly reinforced memories resist pruning; it does not make recall perfect or a memory permanent.
steps.checkpoint: You know why every line of chat is not guaranteed to become a lasting memory.

steps.title: Consolidation organises recent material
steps.narrationDraft: Consolidation & continuity controls grouping, summaries, diary timing and carried impressions. Consolidate Chat after inactivity can run one visible consolidation after an idle Chat turn; continued idling does not repeat it endlessly. LLM summaries can use the model; leave budgets and similarity values at defaults while starting.
steps.checkpoint: You recognise consolidation as upkeep rather than a new task you requested.

steps.title: Embedding settings are an advanced migration choice
steps.narrationDraft: An embedding model turns meaning into numbers used for memory search. The dimension and Vector backend belong to that search representation. Changing an embedding model may require re-embedding old memories. Make a complete backup, read the offered process and track Health → Check before considering it finished. Do not treat the field as an ordinary chat-model selector.
steps.checkpoint: You know to plan and verify an index change rather than merely typing a new name.

steps.title: Leave personality dynamics alone while learning
steps.narrationDraft: Criticality & edge dynamics tunes advisory moods, boredom, wandering and dream recombination. These are experimental behaviour controls, not ways to guarantee reliability or a particular personality. Begin with working defaults; check real behaviour over time before making one deliberate change.
steps.checkpoint: You know which options are optional advanced tuning.
